findings.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — The OAuth-user-vs-sender check is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet (webhook late, dropped, or failed), so an attacker who finishes OAuth as themselves can pass a victim's guessable installation_id in the query string (which overrides the one bound in state, line 448) and claim it into their org.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (500) for any Integration created by the pipeline, because build_integration only writes sender when state has one (test_basic_flow shows metadata without sender), and ensure_integration overwrites webhook metadata on finish. That breaks reinstall after a Sentry-side uninstall, and breaks every legacy integration.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — The OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a static hash of the view class names (the same constant 9cae5e88... for every user in the tests), so it gives no CSRF protection: an attacker can inject their own GitHub `code` into a victim's pipeline and bind github_authenticated_user to the attacker.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:501 — The identity check compares mutable GitHub `login` strings instead of the immutable sender `id` the webhook also stores, so a renamed or re-registered username can pass or fail the check wrongly.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen and get_user_info run outside the try/except, so a GitHub network error or non-2xx /user response surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of the error() dialog, and the popup never gets a postMessage.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now passes only because its state (ddd023...) doesn't match the signature, so the 404 "installation could not be found" path is no longer tested and the test passes without checking what its name says.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError (500) for Integrations whose metadata has no sender, e.g. ones created through the pipeline's DoesNotExist path (build_integration only sets sender when state has it) or legacy installs, whenever such an Integration is re-linked after its OrganizationIntegration is removed.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a deterministic hash of the pipeline view classes that is the same for every user and session (tests hardcode 9cae5e88...), so the state check at line 412 gives no CSRF/session binding and an attacker's code+state callback is accepted into a victim's pipeline.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen` for the token exchange is outside the try/except, so network errors (ConnectionError/SSLError/Timeout) escape as unhandled 500s instead of rendering the error page (OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token catches these).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info` makes a network call and raises on non-2xx/connection failure (e.g. revoked token, GitHub outage) with no handling, so the view 500s instead of returning `error()`.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When no Integration row exists yet (webhook delayed or failed), `next_step()` runs without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installation's sender, so the PR's sender check is skipped and anyone with an enumerable installation_id can claim that installation.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:392 — test_installation_not_found now sends a wrong state (ddd023d8...), so it asserts on the state-mismatch error and no longer covers the build_integration 404 "installation could not be found" path.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:415 — OAuthLoginView re-implements OAuth2CallbackView's token-param building and token exchange/parsing inline (the "similar to OAuth2CallbackView..." comments admit it), so two token-exchange paths must now be kept in sync instead of reusing or subclassing the identity OAuth2 views.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:393 — Integration code creates GitHubIdentityProvider directly and pulls its OAuth client id/secret/authorize/access-token URLs, which couples the integration pipeline to identity-provider internals.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:385 — test_installation_not_found now asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." (triggered by a deliberately wrong state), so the test name no longer matches what it checks, the build_integration 404 "could not be found" path is left untested, and the first resp assignment is dead.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — New module-level helper has the very generic name `error` and no type hints on request/org/return; a name like `render_github_install_error` with typed params would read better and avoid shadowing-style confusion.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:141 — _(error_short)` wraps a variable, so the literals passed at call sites (lines 132, 471, 488) are no longer marked for gettext extraction; before the diff they were `_()`-wrapped literals.
src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:390 — OAuthLoginView.dispatch leaves `pipeline` untyped, while GitHubInstallation.dispatch in the same file declares `pipeline: Pipeline`.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:149 — get_document_origin's parameter is untyped and named `org`, but it actually receives the active organization context (it reads `org.organization`), which makes the name misleading.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — The OAuth authorize URL query string is built by hand with an f-string (no urlencode, redirect_uri not escaped), and the tests lock in that unencoded form, so the code is brittle to change.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — A broad `except Exception` silently swallows token-response read/parse failures with no logging, so OAuth failures show up only as a generic error page and are hard to diagnose.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — The same Integration is fetched twice by external_id (lines 478 and 494), each time with different status filtering, and installation_id is bound in both OAuthLoginView and GitHubInstallation, which splits and blurs responsibility between the two views.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:242 — The magic pipeline-signature state "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" and the code are copy-pasted across many tests (and the auth check uses the positional responses.calls[2]), so any change to signature or call ordering breaks tests in many places; a shared helper/constant would fix this.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen token exchange sits outside the try block, so ConnectionError/Timeout/SSLError when GitHub is slow or down becomes an unhandled 500 in the install popup instead of the error page (OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token catches these).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info is called unguarded and raises on non-2xx/network/JSON errors (e.g. GitHub /user 401/5xx or rate limiting), producing a 500 rather than a rendered failure response.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for existing Integrations whose metadata has no sender (build_integration only sets it when state has a sender), so reinstalling such an orphaned integration returns a 500.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — GitHub token-exchange error payloads (bad_verification_code, incorrect_client_credentials, access_denied with no code) are dropped with a bare except and no logging or metrics, so misconfiguration and outages look like forged requests and are hard to diagnose.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a static md5 of pipeline class names identical for every user/session (tests hardcode 9cae5e88... across users/orgs), so it gives no CSRF protection and lets an attacker inject their own `code` into a victim's pipeline (login CSRF binding attacker's GitHub login).

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When no Integration row exists yet for the attacker-supplied `installation_id` (webhook not yet processed, delayed, or failed), the flow calls `next_step()` without the new sender-login check, so the user-match check can be bypassed and someone else's installation linked to the attacker's org.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — The authorize URL is built with f-string concatenation, and `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` are not URL-encoded; it should use `urlencode` to prevent parameter injection or malformed redirect_uri if these values ever contain reserved characters.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is read with no guard, so existing Integrations without `sender` metadata (e.g. created through the pipeline path) raise KeyError/500 instead of a clean verification failure.

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now fails via OAuth state mismatch (arbitrary state "ddd023...") so the 404 stub is dead and build_integration's "installation could not be found" branch is no longer tested at all

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Hardcoded state "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" is md5 of the pipeline view class paths, so tests enshrine a deterministic user-independent OAuth state (no test asserts per-session/unguessable state) and break on any view rename; exact query equality also locks in an un-urlencoded redirect_uri

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — No test covers an existing Integration without "sender" metadata (pipeline-created, as test_basic_flow shows) and no OrganizationIntegration, which raises KeyError/500; test_github_installed_on_another_org deletes the Integration too (test line 365), sidestepping this path

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:398 — No positive-control test where the webhook-created Integration's sender matches the OAuth login and install succeeds, so the legitimate direct-from-GitHub install path gated by the new check is untested

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic "Invalid installation request." shared by five error branches (state mismatch, no access_token, no login, inactive integration, user mismatch), so it can pass through the wrong branch

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — OAuthLoginView failure branches have no dedicated tests: missing code, token exchange failure/no access_token, get_user_info HTTP error (uncaught, likely 500), and response missing "login"

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:117 — OAuth token and /user mocks answer any request, and no test checks that code/client_id/client_secret were posted or that /user was called with the exchanged token, so they only prove the mocks work

tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:423 — Hardcoded webhook HMAC "sha1=d184e..." is tied to the exact json.dumps bytes of the mutated fixture and the secret; compute it in the test instead of hardcoding
tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — Auth-header check moved from responses.calls[0] to calls[2], so it depends on call order and on how many OAuth mock calls happen first

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:481 — The OAuth-user-vs-sender check is skipped when the Integration row doesn't exist yet (webhook late, dropped, or failed), so an attacker who finishes OAuth as themselves can pass a victim's guessable installation_id in the query string (which overrides the one bound in state, line 448) and claim it into their org.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, `installation_id` is taken from `request.GET` preferentially over the pipeline state (`request.GET.get("installation_id", pipeline.fetch_state("installation_id"))`), so a callback request can override the state-bound installation id. The OAuth-user-vs-sender validation only happens in the branch where an `Integration` row exists (it fetches `Integration.objects.get(..., status=ACTIVE)` and compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`). If `Integration.DoesNotExist` earlier (no row yet), the code returns `pipeline.next_step()` without any sender/installer check, matching the finding that the check is skipped when the Integration row doesn’t exist.

That breaks reinstall after a Sentry-side uninstall, and breaks every legacy integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:501 — The identity check compares mutable GitHub `login` strings instead of the immutable sender `id` the webhook also stores, so a renamed or re-registered username can pass or fail the check wrongly.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the new authenticity check compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` (bound from OAuth `/user` `login`) against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. GitHub `login` is a mutable username, so this check can incorrectly fail for the same user after a rename, and it’s a weaker identity binding than comparing an immutable user identifier (the webhook sender payload typically includes an `id`, and `/user` can return `id` as well). Thus the diff introduces a real correctness/security fragility by keying the verification to `login` rather than an immutable identifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen and get_user_info run outside the try/except, so a GitHub network error or non-2xx /user response surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of the error() dialog, and the popup never gets a postMessage.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, `req = safe_urlopen(...)` is executed before the `try:` block, so any exception from `safe_urlopen` (e.g., network error) will bypass the error dialog and bubble up as a 500. Additionally, `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is also outside any `try/except`; if `get_user_info` raises on a failed/non-2xx `/user` request, it will likewise produce an unhandled 500 instead of returning `error(...)` (the postMessage dialog). The only guarded section is decoding/parsing the access token response via `safe_urlread`/`parse_qsl`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now passes only because its state (ddd023...) doesn't match the signature, so the 404 "installation could not be found" path is no longer tested and the test passes without checking what its name says.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_installation_not_found`, the updated flow now hits `OAuthLoginView` first. The test’s second request uses `state=ddd023...`, which does not match `pipeline.signature`, so `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` returns `error(..., "Invalid installation request.")` before `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` runs. The assertion was changed to check for `"Invalid installation request."`, meaning the original “installation could not be found” behavior is no longer exercised by this test despite the test name implying it is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a deterministic hash of the pipeline view classes that is the same for every user and session (tests hardcode 9cae5e88...), so the state check at line 412 gives no CSRF/session binding and an attacker's code+state callback is accepted into a victim's pipeline.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the OAuth `state` is set to `pipeline.signature` and later validated by direct equality against the same `pipeline.signature`. The accompanying tests assert a fixed, hardcoded `state` value (`9cae5e88...`) in the redirect URL, indicating this value is deterministic/predictable rather than per-session random. Using a predictable `state` defeats OAuth CSRF protection because it does not bind the callback to a specific user/session/request; an attacker can supply a valid `code` with the known `state` and satisfy the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen` for the token exchange is outside the try/except, so network errors (ConnectionError/SSLError/Timeout) escape as unhandled 500s instead of rendering the error page (OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token catches these).

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, the token exchange does `req = safe_urlopen(url=..., data=data)` before the try/except that only wraps `safe_urlread(req)` and parsing. If `safe_urlopen` raises (e.g., connection/SSL/timeout), it will bypass the error handling and likely surface as an unhandled 500 instead of returning the integration-failed page via `error(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info` makes a network call and raises on non-2xx/connection failure (e.g. revoked token, GitHub outage) with no handling, so the view 500s instead of returning `error()`.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, after validating `access_token`, the code calls `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` with no `try/except` around it. Since this is an external GitHub user-info fetch (network I/O) and there is no error handling for exceptions at this point (unlike the subsequent parsing step which is wrapped), any exception from `get_user_info` (e.g., connection error/HTTP error) would bubble up and 500 the view instead of returning `error()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When no Integration row exists yet (webhook delayed or failed), `next_step()` runs without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installation's sender, so the PR's sender check is skipped and anyone with an enumerable installation_id can claim that installation.

adjudication.rationale: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the sender/authenticated-user check is only executed in the branch where an ACTIVE Integration row already exists (it fetches `integration = Integration.objects.get(... status=ACTIVE)` and compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` to `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`). If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code immediately does `return pipeline.next_step()` without any comparison, so the new protection is bypassed in the “no Integration row yet” path (e.g., webhook delayed). The finding’s core claim (check skipped when Integration missing) is directly supported by the diff; the exploitability phrasing is plausible given the skipped gate.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:392 — test_installation_not_found now sends a wrong state (ddd023d8...), so it asserts on the state-mismatch error and no longer covers the build_integration 404 "installation could not be found" path.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_installation_not_found`, the flow was changed to first GET `setup_path` with `installation_id`, then GET `setup_path` with `code` and a hardcoded `state` (`ddd023d8...`) and assert `"Invalid installation request."`. With the new pipeline ordering (`get_pipeline_views` returns `[OAuthLoginView(), GitHubInstallation()]`), the initial `installation_id` request (no `state`) is handled by `OAuthLoginView` and redirects to GitHub authorize, and the follow-up request with a mismatched `state` is rejected in `OAuthLoginView` before reaching `GitHubInstallation` / any installation lookup. So the test no longer exercises the prior "installation could not be found" (404) path; it now covers state-mismatch/authenticity failure instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:415 — OAuthLoginView re-implements OAuth2CallbackView's token-param building and token exchange/parsing inline (the "similar to OAuth2CallbackView..." comments admit it), so two token-exchange paths must now be kept in sync instead of reusing or subclassing the identity OAuth2 views.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` which manually constructs the token request payload (`data = {"code": ..., "client_id": ..., "client_secret": ...}`), calls `safe_urlopen` to `ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url()`, and parses the response via `safe_urlread(...).decode(...)` + `dict(parse_qsl(body))`. The inline comments explicitly note this is "similar to OAuth2CallbackView.get_token_params" and "similar to OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token", indicating duplication of OAuth token-exchange logic rather than reuse/subclassing. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue created by the change, not a directly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:393 — Integration code creates GitHubIdentityProvider directly and pulls its OAuth client id/secret/authorize/access-token URLs, which couples the integration pipeline to identity-provider internals.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` which directly instantiates `GitHubIdentityProvider()` and calls its OAuth-specific methods (`get_oauth_client_id()`, `get_oauth_client_secret()`, `get_oauth_authorize_url()`, `get_oauth_access_token_url()`). This is a concrete coupling of the integration setup pipeline (`src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py`) to identity-provider internals introduced by the change, and is an architectural/scope concern rather than a verifiable functional defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:385 — test_installation_not_found now asserts the generic "Invalid installation request." (triggered by a deliberately wrong state), so the test name no longer matches what it checks, the build_integration 404 "could not be found" path is left untested, and the first resp assignment is dead.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_installation_not_found`, the test now makes two GETs: first with `installation_id` and assigns `resp` but never asserts on it (dead assignment), then a second request with a deliberately wrong `state` (`ddd...`) and asserts `Invalid installation request.`. That exercises the new OAuth state validation in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (`if request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature: return error(...)`), not an "installation not found" path, so the test name no longer matches its behavior and the prior "could not be found" scenario is no longer covered by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:129 — New module-level helper has the very generic name `error` and no type hints on request/org/return; a name like `render_github_install_error` with typed params would read better and avoid shadowing-style confusion.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new module-level helper `def error(request, org, ...)` without type hints, and the name is somewhat generic, but this is a style/readability nit rather than a specific, nontrivial review issue grounded in behavior. There is no demonstrated shadowing/confusion or functional problem in the diff attributable to the name or missing annotations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:141 — _(error_short)` wraps a variable, so the literals passed at call sites (lines 132, 471, 488) are no longer marked for gettext extraction; before the diff they were `_()`-wrapped literals.

adjudication.rationale: The new `error()` helper wraps `error_short` via `_(error_short)` where `error_short` is a runtime variable. In the diff, the call sites pass plain string literals (e.g. `error_short="GitHub installation pending deletion."` and `error_short="Github installed on another Sentry organization."`) without `_()` wrapping, and the default `error_short` is also an unwrapped literal in the function signature. Gettext extraction typically only picks up `_("...")` literal patterns, so these messages will no longer be extracted/translated compared to the previous inline `_()`-wrapped literals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:390 — OAuthLoginView.dispatch leaves `pipeline` untyped, while GitHubInstallation.dispatch in the same file declares `pipeline: Pipeline`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `OAuthLoginView.dispatch(self, request: Request, pipeline)` lacks a type annotation for `pipeline`, while `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` declares `pipeline: Pipeline`. However, this is only a typing/style inconsistency; the code will run the same in Python/Django, and nothing in the diff indicates type checking is enforced such that this would cause a functional failure. It’s not a verifiable defect or substantive review issue based on the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:149 — get_document_origin's parameter is untyped and named `org`, but it actually receives the active organization context (it reads `org.organization`), which makes the name misleading.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `def get_document_origin(org) -> str:` using `org.organization`, so `org` is indeed some active-organization context object (e.g., `self.active_organization`). The finding complains about an untyped parameter name being misleading, which is a style/readability nit rather than a verifiable defect or substantial review issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — The OAuth authorize URL query string is built by hand with an f-string (no urlencode, redirect_uri not escaped), and the tests lock in that unencoded form, so the code is brittle to change.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch the authorize redirect URL is constructed manually via an f-string: `...?client_id=...&state=...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` (no urlencode). The new test `assert_setup_flow` then asserts the *exact* raw query string including the unescaped `redirect_uri=http://testserver/...`, effectively locking parameter ordering/escaping. This is brittle/maintenance-risk (e.g., if redirect_uri ever contains characters needing encoding, or if encoding/order changes), but not a clearly verifiable functional break from the diff alone because the current redirect_uri has no `&`/`?` and many servers accept `:/` unescaped in query values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — A broad `except Exception` silently swallows token-response read/parse failures with no logging, so OAuth failures show up only as a generic error page and are hard to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds OAuthLoginView where the token exchange response is read/parsed inside `try: body = safe_urlread(req).decode("utf-8"); payload = dict(parse_qsl(body))` and then `except Exception: payload = {}` (around the newly added code in OAuthLoginView). There is no logging/metrics on that exception path, and the subsequent `if "access_token" not in payload: return error(...)` yields only a generic failure page. This is a diagnosability/observability concern introduced by the change, not a direct correctness defect since failures are still handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:494 — The same Integration is fetched twice by external_id (lines 478 and 494), each time with different status filtering, and installation_id is bound in both OAuthLoginView and GitHubInstallation, which splits and blurs responsibility between the two views.

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the code does fetch `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` inside the `installations_exist` check, and later fetches again as `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` for the sender/login verification. That is a real, diff-grounded duplication with potentially inconsistent selection criteria (status-filtered vs not). Also, `installation_id` is bound in both `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` (when present in GET) and again in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` (from GET or pipeline state), which is a concrete responsibility split introduced by the new pipeline step. This is more of an architectural/clarity/perf concern than a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:242 — The magic pipeline-signature state "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" and the code are copy-pasted across many tests (and the auth check uses the positional responses.calls[2]), so any change to signature or call ordering breaks tests in many places; a shared helper/constant would fix this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes the pipeline signature state string "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" and the OAuth code in multiple test cases (e.g., assert_setup_flow and several tests building setup_path_2). It also updates the auth assertion to rely on a specific call index (responses.calls[2]) after adding two new HTTP calls, making tests sensitive to future changes in pipeline signature generation or request ordering. This is a concrete maintainability/test brittleness issue introduced by the changes, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:423 — safe_urlopen token exchange sits outside the try block, so ConnectionError/Timeout/SSLError when GitHub is slow or down becomes an unhandled 500 in the install popup instead of the error page (OAuth2CallbackView.exchange_token catches these).

adjudication.rationale: In the new `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the token exchange call `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is executed before the `try:` block. The `try/except` only wraps `safe_urlread(req).decode(...)` and parsing, so network/SSL/timeout exceptions raised by `safe_urlopen` would bypass the error handling and likely surface as an unhandled 500 instead of rendering the integration-failed error page. This matches the finding and is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:434 — get_user_info is called unguarded and raises on non-2xx/network/JSON errors (e.g. GitHub /user 401/5xx or rate limiting), producing a 500 rather than a rendered failure response.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added OAuthLoginView.dispatch, `authenticated_user_info = get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called without any `try/except` (unlike the preceding token parsing which is guarded). From the diff alone we can verify the lack of guarding; if `get_user_info` performs an HTTP request/JSON parse and can raise on network/non-2xx/parse errors, those exceptions would bubble and bypass the intended `error(...)` rendering path, potentially yielding a 500. The diff does not show `get_user_info`'s implementation, so the claim that it definitely raises on those conditions is not directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError for existing Integrations whose metadata has no sender (build_integration only sets it when state has a sender), so reinstalling such an orphaned integration returns a 500.

src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:428 — GitHub token-exchange error payloads (bad_verification_code, incorrect_client_credentials, access_denied with no code) are dropped with a bare except and no logging or metrics, so misconfiguration and outages look like forged requests and are hard to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the token exchange response is parsed inside a broad `except Exception` that sets `payload = {}` with no logging/metrics, and any non-`access_token` response (including OAuth error fields like `error=bad_verification_code` or `access_denied`) is treated identically via `return error(...)` (generic “Invalid installation request”). This makes real OAuth/config/outage issues hard to diagnose, but it doesn’t clearly break correctness beyond returning a generic failure page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:402 — OAuth `state` is `pipeline.signature`, a static md5 of pipeline class names identical for every user/session (tests hardcode 9cae5e88... across users/orgs), so it gives no CSRF protection and lets an attacker inject their own `code` into a victim's pipeline (login CSRF binding attacker's GitHub login).

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the OAuth `state` is set to `pipeline.signature` when initiating the GitHub authorize redirect, and later validated by simple equality against `pipeline.signature`. The diff provides no per-request/session entropy (no random nonce stored in session/state), and the updated tests assert a fixed `state=9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3` value in the redirect URL across different org/user flows, indicating `pipeline.signature` is deterministic rather than unique per user/session. Using a deterministic value for OAuth `state` removes CSRF protection for the OAuth callback and could allow cross-user request injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:482 — When no Integration row exists yet for the attacker-supplied `installation_id` (webhook not yet processed, delayed, or failed), the flow calls `next_step()` without the new sender-login check, so the user-match check can be bypassed and someone else's installation linked to the attacker's org.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` only enforces the new authenticated-user vs `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` check in the branch where an ACTIVE `Integration` already exists (the later `Integration.objects.get(..., status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)` block). If `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `Integration.DoesNotExist`, the code immediately does `return pipeline.next_step()` without any sender-login validation. The finding’s “bypass” impact depends on pipeline behavior and webhook timing (not shown in this diff), so the security consequence isn’t fully verifiable here, but the edge case (no Integration row yet => no user-match check) is real and grounded in the added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:408 — The authorize URL is built with f-string concatenation, and `client_id`, `state` and `redirect_uri` are not URL-encoded; it should use `urlencode` to prevent parameter injection or malformed redirect_uri if these values ever contain reserved characters.

adjudication.rationale: In `OAuthLoginView.dispatch`, the authorize redirect URL is constructed via f-string concatenation: `...authorize_url()}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}` without using `urlencode`. This is verifiably true in the diff. However, the specific values shown are controlled/generated (`github_client_id` from provider config, `state` from `pipeline.signature`, and `redirect_uri` from `absolute_uri(reverse(...))`) and are not shown to include characters like `&`/`=` that would actually cause parameter injection or a malformed URL in this change, making it more of a robustness/hardening concern than a demonstrable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` is read with no guard, so existing Integrations without `sender` metadata (e.g. created through the pipeline path) raise KeyError/500 instead of a clean verification failure.
matched_golden_ids: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the code reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] without verifying the "sender" key exists, leading to a KeyError (and resulting 500) for integrations created without sender metadata.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:396 — test_installation_not_found now fails via OAuth state mismatch (arbitrary state "ddd023...") so the 404 stub is dead and build_integration's "installation could not be found" branch is no longer tested at all

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` returns `error(...)` immediately when `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature`. The updated `test_installation_not_found` now hits `/extensions/github/setup/` with `state="ddd023..."`, which (per other tests asserting the signature is `9cae5e...`) will trigger this early "Invalid installation request" path before any installation lookup/build step runs. As a result, the previous behavior asserted by the test ("The GitHub installation could not be found.") is no longer exercised, so that installation-not-found branch is no longer covered by this test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:235 — Hardcoded state "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" is md5 of the pipeline view class paths, so tests enshrine a deterministic user-independent OAuth state (no test asserts per-session/unguessable state) and break on any view rename; exact query equality also locks in an un-urlencoded redirect_uri

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the test asserting an exact redirect query string including a hardcoded `state=9cae5e...` and a literal `redirect_uri=http://testserver/extensions/github/setup/` (tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py around the new assertions in `assert_setup_flow`). This makes the test brittle (it will break if the pipeline signature generation or view ordering changes) and it encodes expectations about the OAuth URL construction rather than asserting higher-level properties (e.g., that a state is present and consistent across the flow). However, the finding’s claim that the state is specifically an MD5 of pipeline view class paths is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:503 — No test covers an existing Integration without "sender" metadata (pipeline-created, as test_basic_flow shows) and no OrganizationIntegration, which raises KeyError/500; test_github_installed_on_another_org deletes the Integration too (test line 365), sidestepping this path

adjudication.rationale: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, after fetching an existing active `Integration` (`Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id, status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)`), the new authenticity check unconditionally indexes `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. If an existing `Integration` record lacks `sender` (or `login`) in `metadata`—which is not prevented/validated anywhere in this diff—this will raise `KeyError` and likely 500 instead of rendering the intended error page. The diff introduces this unguarded access and no test in the added/modified cases covers the missing-`sender` metadata path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:398 — No positive-control test where the webhook-created Integration's sender matches the OAuth login and install succeeds, so the legitimate direct-from-GitHub install path gated by the new check is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new security gate in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` for the case where an `Integration` already exists but no `OrganizationIntegration` exists: it fetches the authenticated GitHub user from pipeline state (`pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")`) and requires it to equal `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, otherwise it returns `error(...)`. The new tests include a negative-control mismatch case (`test_github_user_mismatch`) but there is no corresponding positive-control test exercising the same branch where the webhook-created Integration sender *matches* the OAuth login and the flow proceeds successfully. Existing success tests (e.g., `assert_setup_flow`) appear to cover the path where the Integration does not yet exist (leading to `pipeline.next_step()` earlier), not the new "Integration exists" branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:454 — test_github_user_mismatch asserts only the generic "Invalid installation request." shared by five error branches (state mismatch, no access_token, no login, inactive integration, user mismatch), so it can pass through the wrong branch

adjudication.rationale: In `test_github_user_mismatch`, the test only asserts the presence of the generic text `"Invalid installation request."`. In the diff, multiple distinct failure paths return `error(...)` with the same default `error_short`/message: OAuth state mismatch (`OAuthLoginView`), missing `access_token`, missing `login`, missing/INACTIVE `Integration` (`Integration.objects.get(..., status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE)`), and the intended GitHub user mismatch check (`github_authenticated_user` vs `integration.metadata['sender']['login']`). Because the test doesn’t assert anything that uniquely identifies the mismatch branch (or that earlier steps succeeded), it could pass even if it hit a different error branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:412 — OAuthLoginView failure branches have no dedicated tests: missing code, token exchange failure/no access_token, get_user_info HTTP error (uncaught, likely 500), and response missing "login"

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new logic in `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` with multiple failure branches (`state` mismatch, token exchange/parse yielding no `access_token`, `get_user_info` result missing `login`). The updated tests cover the happy path and the `state` mismatch case (`test_installation_not_found` now expects "Invalid installation request.") and a later mismatch check in `GitHubInstallation` (`test_github_user_mismatch`), but there are no tests for several OAuthLoginView-specific failure paths (e.g., missing `code`, token endpoint not returning `access_token`, or `/user` returning no `login`). Also, `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is not wrapped in a try/except in this diff, so an exception there would bubble up; the diff does not add coverage for that behavior either.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:117 — OAuth token and /user mocks answer any request, and no test checks that code/client_id/client_secret were posted or that /user was called with the exchanged token, so they only prove the mocks work

adjudication.rationale: In `tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py` `_stub_github()` registers a POST to `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` with a fixed `body=f"access_token={access_token}"` and a GET to `/user` returning `{"login": "octocat"}`. The updated tests (e.g. `assert_setup_flow`) only verify the redirect and later pipeline behavior, and adjust call index (`responses.calls[2]`) but never assert the POST parameters included `code/client_id/client_secret` nor that the `/user` request used the exchanged token (e.g. `Authorization: token ...`). So the tests don't validate the new OAuth exchange logic beyond the mocks being hit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:423 — Hardcoded webhook HMAC "sha1=d184e..." is tied to the exact json.dumps bytes of the mutated fixture and the secret; compute it in the test instead of hardcoding

adjudication.rationale: In `test_github_user_mismatch`, the webhook request uses a hardcoded `HTTP_X_HUB_SIGNATURE="sha1=d184e..."` while the posted body is `json.dumps(webhook_event)` after mutating the fixture (`installation.id` and `sender.login`). Since GitHub webhook HMACs are computed over the exact raw request bytes, this hardcoded signature is brittle and can break if serialization details or the fixture change; computing the signature from the actual JSON bytes in the test would make it robust. This is a test-quality issue rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py:257 — Auth-header check moved from responses.calls[0] to calls[2], so it depends on call order and on how many OAuth mock calls happen first

adjudication.rationale: In tests/sentry/integrations/github/test_integration.py the assertion was changed from `responses.calls[0]` to `responses.calls[2]` (see `auth_header = responses.calls[2].request.headers[...]`). This test now implicitly relies on the exact number/order of preceding mocked HTTP calls introduced by the new OAuth flow (POST to `/login/oauth/access_token` and GET `/user` were added in `_stub_github`). Any future change in the OAuth/login sequence or additional requests would break the test without indicating a real regression, so it’s a fragile, diff-grounded test issue rather than an app defect.
